They need Project Engineers in 4 location over 4 different Vendors. Aerohead - Los Alamitos, CA - They Build the core stage of the Feed Lines. Need someone with Structural Feed lines and NDT Experience. Experience in Building Hardware. Has some experience in Stress Fracture nondestructive evaluation. Just need to be able to speak stress. Mechanical Engineering background working with Stress and Fracture Engineers. General Dynamics - Lincoln NB - They do the COPV's (Composite Overwrap Pressure Vessels) of the upper stage and core stage of the rocket. COPV's are a metallic tank wrapped in composite fibers. They hold the helium on the space craft. Want someone with Mechanical/propulsion engineering background that has pressure vessel exp. Nu Space - Long Beach, CA - They do a separate tank for the exploration upper stage. This is what's called a Hydrazine Mono Prop System. Some one with Mono Propellent Propulsion System background, Hypergolics, or Hydrazine. Someone with Mechanical Engineering with Propulsion Satellite experience. Pacific Scientific (Pac SCi) - Chandler, AZ - Building the Core Stage and EUS (Exploration Upper Stage) of the Safe and Arm mechanism. This is a device that arms the rocket if it is over land so it can explode before it hits land. It's a component that takes the aircraft from a safe position to an Armed position. Need Someone with Pyrotechnical system Background or Ordinance Position background. Someone with Electromechanical device experience. She also connect me with Anthony Hankinson (Program Quality Manager) and Alyssa Helwig ( Senior Manager, Space Launch System Production Engineering ) for there Michoud Assembly Facility. They need people over there because of the recent attrition they have gone through. Need to set up a meeting with both of them this week.

Full_Note: Perton - DFAS - Greg Nash - Program Manager - Scheduled Call to discuss his req's - Tuesday, Jan. 6th at 10am ET RTP: - Had a nice holiday break, went to see family in Missouri - today is his one-year anniversary starting this role (Jan 6th) - mentioned a big fishing trip in Canada he's going with high school friends in late March RTB: - wanted to discuss his customers' urgent need of a Full-Time - COBOL Mainframe Programmer to support their payroll application - I asked why they opened this position and why is it so urgent = Greg said, that DFAS was supposed to have this done in December, and they didn't do it, so it's an urgent need and they're fighting from behind on some things and need to get this person onboarded - 6 month contract to hire - open to onsite and remote candidates - job is based out of Indianpolis, Indiana - said he'll have a need for 2 more COBOL Mainframe Developers in February too and for us to keep pumping him COBOL candidates as he believes he'll need at least 1/month - Process = Submit to Greg, then schedule call with him, then he submits to DFAS to schedule an interview - he admitted that he's at DFAS's mercy, doesn't have any input, doesn't directly know their day-to-day responsibilities, he's mostly there to provide warm bodies - he hasn't received any resumes yet, said we will probably come across candidates that we've submitted in the past - Key is to have the IDMS experience (it's an old school database) - most of the candidates will be older as COBOL is old programming, most of his employees are 60+ years of age and last year he hired a 78 year old - hired 10 COBOL programmers last year due to attrition - said most of them are older, and when they're done, they're done - they just leave and/or quit, and he also believes the AGILE environment is pushing them away as many don't like to be micro-managed - int avail = Thurs and Fri 3pm ET and 4pm ET - start date = takes a month from offer, some times more - AGILE environment - Top SKills = COBOL exp (2-4 yrs), IDMS, Agile environment and ADSO (a strong nice to have) - no active clearance is required to start, but must have ability to obtain a PUBLIC TRUST - projected start date = Mid to late February

Full_Note: SAIC - FAA - ISC Meeting with Michael. He is located just north of the Twin Cities, 10 degrees out there right now. Born and raised there, had a good Thanksgiving and just getting back into the swing of things. He is the Technical Services Team Manager for the FAA - ISC program. ISC stands for Integrated Service Center, and they support the FAA. Part of CLIN 2, and there are other CLINs like depot, onsite, etc. He has been on the program for four years. Turn over rate has greatly decreased over the last few years from 7 percent to 2.2 percent. Michael's counterpart is Robin Toulen - she is the Service Delivery Manager for the remote support. Burt is the Program Manager. 93 individuals on the Service Desk team. 140-150 individuals on the ISC team. Public Trust, need to get the FAA clearance. This is usually what holds up onboarding as it can take 6-12 weeks to get. The Service Center is 24/7, so shifts all around the clock. Shifts operate on East Coast hours. Usually, the night shift is 12 am to 8:30 AM. If they work a weekend, he usually gives them the option to do 5x8 or 4x10. The Service Desk is Level 0 technically. Take recent college grads or anyone looking to get into the industry. Need to want to be in a customer support role. Start people every three weeks, all new hires on the same day. 2 weeks of classroom training from 8-4:30, and then they switch to do some calls and tickets (not metric tracked) for another week. Hit the ground running on that fourth week. Looking for these people to stay on long term. No vacancies right now, but happy to interview now and make contingent offers. Would interview in December to bring someone on in January. Would be the typical service desk profile. F/U: sending us details on the roles and interview process, said that Prasad would be the one for monthly connects and he would hop on as needed

Full_Note: SAIC - FAA - ISC Meeting with Michael. He is located just north of the Twin Cities, 10 degrees out there right now. Born and raised there, had a good Thanksgiving and just getting back into the swing of things. He is the Technical Services Team Manager for the FAA - ISC program. ISC stands for Integrated Service Center, and they support the FAA. Part of CLIN 2, and there are other CLINs like depot, onsite, etc. He has been on the program for four years. Turn over rate has greatly decreased over the last few years from 7 percent to 2.2 percent. Michael's counterpart is Robin Toulen - she is the Service Delivery Manager for the remote support. Burt is the Program Manager. 93 individuals on the Service Desk team. 140-150 individuals on the ISC team. Public Trust, need to get the FAA clearance. This is usually what holds up onboarding as it can take 6-12 weeks to get. The Service Center is 24/7, so shifts all around the clock. Shifts operate on East Coast hours. Usually, the night shift is 12 am to 8:30 AM. If they work a weekend, he usually gives them the option to do 5x8 or 4x10. The Service Desk is Level 0 technically. Take recent college grads or anyone looking to get into the industry. Need to want to be in a customer support role. Start people every three weeks, all new hires on the same day. 2 weeks of classroom training from 8-4:30, and then they switch to do some calls and tickets (not metric tracked) for another week. Hit the ground running on that fourth week. Looking for these people to stay on long term. No vacancies right now, but happy to interview now and make contingent offers. Would interview in December to bring someone on in January. Would be the typical service desk profile. F/U: sending us details on the roles and interview process, said that Prasad would be the one for monthly connects and he would hop on as needed

Full_Note: Leidos - GSMOII - Network Team Lead - Said his weekend was cold and rainy - out of Scott AFB - His team supports MDA (missile defense agency) - They do white glove service, engineering and all internal networking and everything transport related for DISA for the MDA - They are 24/7 ops and a customer facing NOC -when he hires people he look smore at personable skills and the technical experience isn't as important - because of the customer facing aspect - said he needs someone that at least has some sort of hands-on experience and certifications are always helpful (CCNA, ITL) - There are 32 people on his team, 22 people of those people are on the "floor" - Right now they are 50/50 between Scott AFB and Hill AFB - He said he likes to keep it at 10 and 10 at each site at all times - He said he rarely hires direct and the only people that are FT Leidos are contractors that converted and there are only a handful of them - He gravitates towards subs because of obvious reasons, we vet them better and he doesn't have to spend as much time handling things - He likes to move quickly, once the req is out, he likes to pick 5 or 6 candidates to interview that week and make a decision from there - says he always lets becky know on mondays or whenever he is aware of the position and becky will let people know before the role comes out on Friday - It takes about 4 months to train these people, so as soon as they lose someone they are instantly behind 4 months - LCAT 62 and 63 is what he typically hires at, rarely will use 61 - Said he doesn't have a preference on the competitors of ours -Has 7-9 attrition a year, so he hires about once a month - Reason for attrition is people leave for other positions in the building and sometimes has been from not understanding the job they would be doing Org Wise: - He reports to Rich King, along with Paul Stancil who does AISR and "George" who does TRIP and "Zach", there is only a handful of direct reports to Rich - Rich has 2 deputy's - Josh and Damian and they each have their own reports

Full_Note: GDIT - Resource Manager - JUSTIFIED - Monthly JUSTIFIED meeting w/ Heather and the team to discuss the following topics: Effect the Government shutdown is having on the contract. The following areas are being affected by the shutdown: Start Dates for new hires. The security team on the government side has taken a hit as many of the team are not working due to the shutdown. Mentioned only a handful of the government security team is working. This has caused delays in onboarding due to not being able to brief contractors for their SCI. There could be issues with funding for certain CUP’s as the funding for this contract is incremental and there are a few CUP’s whose funding runs out in mid-November. This is causing delays in onboarding as well since GDIT will not bring a new hire onto a team that is running low on funding. This also could affect current contractors if the government shutdown is not over soon. Said some of the CUP’s might have contractors work at-risk or even stop work completely. Pause on the 90 new spots that were slated to be added to the contract in Q4. Mentioned that if the government shutdown continues, the new MOD with the 90 spots will more than likely be pushed to March 2026. Jon Miner has been relieved from his role as the NCR lead and Pam McComas will be taking over duties for the time being. GDIT is actively working to find a replacement but did not provide a timeline of when that will be. Pam has a few candidates in mind and mentioned if the candidates she has in mind fall through, they might allow subs to help with the sourcing.

Mark Trudel – Security background w/ over 25 years of experience in the industry. Eastern region is now the only region with OCONUS work. Cindy Nusbaum – Been w/ GDIT but new to the JUSTIFIED contract. Has a lot of proposal type experience. Pam McComas – Husband’s name is Steve and they have been together for 12 years now. Full_Note: Leidos, SSA, ITSSC: met with Neha this morning, learned a little about her background. She moved to the US from India in 2007 and has lived in Neward, NJ and now lives in the Baltimore area. Gave her an introduction on PTS and went over the work we do with Leidos and HHS. She let me know that she is the deputy pm, and that she directly oversees two different teams, with a total of 65 people. She did not know the breakdown of contractor to fte, but she said its a good mix of both. Current projects they have ongoing are focused on a migration from the domino platform to the Microsoft equivalent platform, while the other team is focused on digital modernization of the visitor intake process at the SSA headquarters in Baltimore. Team comprises mostly developers, as well as analysts, and testers. The majority of the team is onsite, which was forced upon them starting in February. There are still some people remote but they are working to get them onsite full time. Neha participates in interviews but she said she is not considered a hiring manager and does not review resumes herself. They are currently preparing a proposal that will include projects and needs for next year, and she said they will not be doing much hiring until that is approved. She said they anticipate that approval to be received in late september/early october. Set a follow up meeting for the first week of October.

Full_Note: Leidos, NASA, NEST: met with Ray yesterday afternoon, he let me know that he is the CTO for Leidos NASA, overseeing all NASA programs that Leidos is a prime for, as well as a few that they are subs on. He let me know that their attrition is currently below industry standards, but that people are regularly leaving here and there, and that is becoming more common as the program hits the tail end of it's lifecycle. There has also not been much communication from NASA about a new RFP, so they are unsure about what the future will look like right now. Since I already met with Melody, Ray told me to reach out to Kenneth for an introduction, and that he may have a position we can work for him. Set follow up meeting with Ray for a month out.

Full_Note: Leidos, NASA, NEST: Met with Melodey Lawson on Monday, she’s the Manager for Leidos’ NEST program overseeing all Service Delivery Operations for the contract. She’s in Covington, Louisiana working remote, but her main onsite location is Michoud Assembly Facility (MAF) in New Orleans. She let me know that her teams combined are a total of 190 people, and all of which are in positions focused on delivery of services to over 60,000 NASA personnel. These teams are made up of end-user support specialists, hardware specialists (pc technicians), M365 specialists, logistics, incident response, (mostly lower-level positions). End-user support and help desk personnel work remote, while the rest are all onsite. She let me know that most of the engineers and senior leadership are within the Enterprise Operations division. The employees and contractors under her division are more widely distributed across the different NASA locations, which include Orlando, Huntsville, Houston, New Orleans, Stennis, and White Sands facility in New Mexico. She said her most utilized sub is a small named EMCO technologies, asked why they use them and she said they have been partners for a while, and they bring Microsoft and nasa expertise. Told her we’re a Microsoft partner as well and will also contribute to a small business spend. She did not know their small business goal off hand. Had to go, let me know that she doesn’t have any openings for us to help with right now and that they are anticipating that they will be affected by the pending government shutdown. Next meeting in two weeks.

Full_Note: Leidos, NASA, AEGIS: Had an introduction meeting with Heath this morning. He's the Service Integration Manager for Leidos' AEGIS program. He's seated in Huntsville, and oversees a team of 10. His team focuses on change management, configuration management, and SLA management. He stepped into this manager role about a year ago. As a whole, his team manages the integration between the different tool sets that the program utilizes (ITSM - remedy). They were informed that NASA wants them to transition to a new ITSM tool, ServiceNow, and they started that transition at the beginning of last year. However, they are still in the requirements gathering phase currently. Their ServiceNow developers are coming directly from NASA to build out that platform. He let us know that it seems like every six months, smaller, center-based contracts are expiring and are getting rolled onto AEGIS. He gave us the name and number for his boss, Janice Markey. She's the PMO manager for the program and works remote out of Pennsylvania. He confirmed with us that we're an SDVOSB, said that NASA has been making a push for more women owned and service disabled owned small business support. He also gave us the name for the Data Center/Cloud Manager, John Allie. Said that he is leading the effort in which they are consolidating multiple data centers into a more enterprise data center approach. Said he thinks he would be a good POC for us and can use our help. The locations where AEGIS does the most work is Johnson and Kennedy space centers. There's about 1000 people on the contract as a whole and they're on contract year 4 of 10.

Full_Note: Deloitte - Triple Crown - Scored some time on Eric's calendar to discuss the pending SDVOSB for PrimeTS. They have completed their orals and written objectives for the TRIPLECROWN II pursuit and will utilize PTS as a teaming partner utilizing our R&D small business NAICS Code. The DoD Triple Crown II program focuses on bolstering the Air Force (AF) and Combatant Command (CCMD) warfighting capabilities in cyberspace operations. More specifically, it aims to develop and support: Training Intelligence Plans and Exercise Support Cyber Readiness Operations Weapons & Tactics Network Defensive Operations II (TRIPLECROWN II). Air Force Network (AFNET) missions. Cyber Defensive Analysis (CDA) activities. Offensive Cyber Operations (OCO) missions. The program's objective is to provide warfighting commands with skilled cyberspace operations professionals to enhance network defense, offer cyberspace operations support, and ensure mission assurance. The program used a competitive acquisition process to find businesses with relevant expertise. Set up monthly tag-up with Eric. Anticipating is Q1 of the government calendar for the award announcement.

Full_Note: Boeing - LEOS - 1/27/2026  Boeing - ABQ / LEOS Program - Greg Strawder - Sr. EE Design Analysis Engineer (Hiring Manager) and over all Systems Engineer hiring in ABQ - Andreas Rodriguez made introduction for me with Greg.  Next Steps: 1) Greg's emailing us the job descriptions for his Lead Electrical Engineer, Optical and Controls Engineers 2) Greg's connecting with David Barningham to discuss us supporting their Software Engineer openings/needs 3) Scheduling an onsite meeting in ABQ in 2-3 weeks 4) Lead Electrical Engineer position - F/U with me on Max Bill Rate  RTP: - talked about him being an HBCU alum - Tuskegee University - cool to see HBCU more represented in this space  RTB: - Greg reports to Brad Hirasuna - also works in tandem with David Barningham with hiring for ABQ (David's over Software and Greg's over ALL of ABQ, but mostly Systems Engineering) - Need for Controls Engineer - this can be utilized for the program, but not used specifically for the program. (They have a deficit of Controls Engineers at ABQ) - also need Optical Engineers - Prioritize and/or Overstaff Certain Areas (below):  #1A Software - Architect, Lead and Engineers (# 10-15 by end of year) - David Barningham's over these positions - Greg's getting with David and will f/u with me #1B Systems Engineers/Architects (# 5-10 by end of year) - Greg's the HM #2 Optical Engineers (# 2-3) - Greg's the HM #3 Controls Engineers (# 2-3) - Greg's the HM - confirmed what Brad Hirasuna saying he'll need at least 30 Engineers onboarded this calendar year, he'd be OK with that. - - said he'd outsource or do service contracts for some of the remaining SOW (multi-pronged approach to this - but does want to build a core group of Engineers = 60-70 Engineers in total) - if we could find a good Lead Electrical (Design and Analysis) Engineer - would be priority #3 (high priority) = 1 good elite electrical Engineer and also overstaff Systems and Software Engineers - ALL positions are 12 mos. Full_Note: Boeing - BDS - SEIT Organization - Brad Hirasuna - SEIT Leader - Onsite Meeting (Bdg. S30) El Segundo, CA  NEXT STEPS: Email Brad, thank you note, meeting recap (including how we'll reach out to Alex Le to schedule intro and discuss 10 Seal Beach SWE openings) and schedule intro mtg with ABQ's Greg Strawder  RTB: - Currently wrapping up ACR's (Annual Contract Review - started in November '25) - requires a lot of paperwork and takes up a majority of the managers times at Boeing  - Discussed how recently a very large BDS program received an unexpected "stop-work", which ate up a lot of their openings and is why they ultimately did not have the 150 forecasted positions to fill that was previously discussed in November '25 - Big Thing for Brad right now is ABQ (Albuquerque) - we have a DD254 in place  - - Said Greg Strawder is the new Manager leading all hiring efforts in ABQ  - - - Greg has a 30 person push and said they have to get the jobs into Beeline and start working them asap. (Brad wants us to fly out to ABQ and meet with Greg) - - - - Asked if we have an FTE agreement - we do not. Only support Contract or C2H positions - We asked where else we could support: - - He said outside of ABQ, everything else is onesie twosies (I'll remind him that we can support those as well) - -OTHER: Seal Beach (CA) has spots and are currently hiring 10 FTE's (FTE attempts are first for typically 4 weeks, sometimes shorter), but Brad feels they've exhausted their efforts and need to get a staffing plan together with Alex Le (Seal Beach - Responsible for hiring 10 Software Engineers) and should move to 12 months, C2H - check back with Brad on this next week - Boeing is also anticipating winning 2 contracts (one in April, the other around June) - - the one in April is very large (not as big as ESS, but still very big and will need a lot of hiring/surge support) and they'll need to go C2H

Full_Note: Boeing - BDS Org. - ESS Program - Andy Davis - Simulation and Software, Testbed Manager - Scheduled Phone Meeting (In preparation of our in-person meeting with his boss Jon Haritatos)  RTB: - said how he's in the middle of wrapping up ACR's like everyone else, said it really makes being a Manager tough when they take up 75% of his work day for months - he reiterated what other MGR's have mentioned with the large Boeing program receiving a "stop-work", thus releasing a lot of Boeing FTE's, which they've managed to transition into other programs at BDS (which is why they've put a hold on hiring as they've filled many of these spots) - now they're figuring out headcount because they don't want to have too little headcount and when they win new awards be put into a bind, but they also don't have to have too high of headcount and have folks sitting around without work to do - ESS is very healthy, has received good feedback on their progress thus far

Note_Preview: Boeing - BDS - Brad Hirasuna - Chief Engineer / Engineering Leader for all of BDS (Michelle Parker's #2) - (2nd) Onsite Meeting (Bdg. S30) El Segundo, CA  NEXT STEPS: Email Nick, thank you note, meeti
Full_Note: Boeing - BDS - Brad Hirasuna - Chief Engineer / Engineering Leader for all of BDS (Michelle Parker's #2) - (2nd) Onsite Meeting (Bdg. S30) El Segundo, CA  NEXT STEPS: Email Nick, thank you note, meeting recap - check in periodically and report progress and see if he has any areas we could support AND he'd introduce us to Megumi Telles's (SOFTWARE ORG) backfill AND f/u on him saying he'd check with Millenium Space Systems on intorductions  RTB: - His E.A. - Ani Rodriguez walked us to his office  - Said they are focused on ABQ and hiring SIGINT, Radar and Optical - Primarily SIGINT - needs 5-6 = Brad Hirasun and Dennis Gould are over this (I'm working with Dennis) - - Said the SIGINT encompasses 2 types of work: 1) Managing "customer perception" - touches on the BD piece of the role as Boeing is not known for SIGINT work or solutions, so they need to bring in someone with that perception, who the end customer (Space Force, Air Force, Navy) would immediately recognize and know what they bring to the table (SIGINT solutions) and then of course the Payload, Systems Engineering expertise as well (Very rare skillset with the BD, SIGINT and Payload, Systems Engineering expertise) - ABQ has a lot of work supporting multiple programs and are targeting having 50-75 open positions moving forward, not all jobs are out at once - mentioned SOFTWARE Org. leader has been promoted - he'll introduce us to Megumi's backfill (this was just announced this week) - said Megumi's now over Space, Intelligence and Weapons Systems - Software Lead over SLS (Huntsville) - I asked about Millenium Space Systems (this subsidiary) because both Michelle and Nick mentioned back in our Nov. Full_Note: LMCO   re: below ;  Interview sit in  Intro- Ted introduces himself and goes over the core SE & IT org under Space Systems  Went back in time to GBI during Bush administration  Bridging the gap to NGI and why we need it to keep up with our enemy threats initial contract from MDA was with the development from SRR with Raytheon/ Northrop/ Lockheed  PDR with Lockheed beating out Northrop based on tech solution Lifecycle of the program: "middle of CDR season"  Only CDR that matters to Ted is the final with customer (end of year) Prior will be subset CDR with: sensor, kill vehicle, booster   Ted then asks Tanner if he has any questions based on program overview  Ted asks Tanner to introduce himself and why he wants to work on the work on the program  Laughed about the test sites with China Lake and White Sands   Ted dives into technical questions: -have you had full ownership of specifications?  -this is a cleared program, are you ok with no having your phone in the scif? -walk me through your resume example here with test and writing test scripts (walked through Raytheon test fire example with data plotting & the integration with THAAD, Coyote, and Gun Fire). Ted thought this was a good example  -Was your hypersonic program a development program? (yes) -Did you run into anything from legacy systems and/ or inappropriate/ outdated (yes, gives booster example at Mach 12 test versus Mach 10 with testing and verifying)  -what was your most significant presentation/ report? (gave gaza example and presentation to subordinate of Secretary of State)   Ted explains that it's a heavy development program. "the people that made the promises of yesterday are not here for the questions of today" This creates often making comprises between technical and schedule Have you ever had this scenario and how did you deal with it? (yes, gives an example of this week on swing shift)   If you join the team, you'll be joining a diverse group of engineers  When you typically join a new group, how do you build trust? (I am not the smartest person in the room, not afraid to ask questions, and is not afraid to jump in but doesn't want to hold the group back either with the comfortable process)  Thought Tanner answered this well with humility   Lot of documentation: unit specifications, V&V, requirements  In the future we will be onsite testing Can you walk

Full_Note: Leidos, DMDC, DCPDS: met with Dean on Wednesday, told me a little about his holidays and how he's prepping for this storm this week. Confirmed all our employees still doing great. Wasn't able to give a good estimate on when he thinks it will be done just yet. No new needs on his team at this time, said he would give me a heads up if anything new comes up. Told me to keep him in the loop on any power outages or issues with any of our employees working remote once Monday morning comes around.

Full_Note: Leidos, MCEN: met with Erin yesterday afternoon, said that her site visit at Camp Lejeune went great, she was at the airport waiting for her flight back home. Let me know that Leidos has still not identified a backfill for Jace, still planning on opening it back up to us if they continue to struggle.
